g.title: BM4ImplicitFullExecution
g.text: Horizontal: complete lifecycle. Vertical: preparation, numerical solve and accepted-step records.
Blue: public contracts and shared infrastructure. Orange: BM4 method. Green: numerical kernels. Purple: optional observation.
One reduced projection surrounds each complete twelve-stage cycle. N = particles; T = saved times; m = 2N.
Module paths are relative to src/simulation/methods/bm4/ unless stated otherwise.

g.title: Configuration
g.text: Accepted state: z in R^m, m = 2N.
Temporary coupled copies: (u, v) in R^(2m).
One symmetric Hairer projection per full cycle.
All solve the same reduced equation.

g.title: PhaseExecution
g.text: Descend into one complete numerical advance

g.title: Prepare
g.text: uses track_energy=False and binds coupled maps.
Store formulation, initial state and metadata on self.
Initialize the common controller with physical z0.
self.formulation owns the temporary copy maps.
No integration history is allocated here.

g.title: RunMethod
g.text: SAME NUMERICAL CLASS / ONE INSTANCE PER EXECUTION
No separate context or callback-based method record.
Construct another instance for another integration.
Completed runs cannot re-enter the global driver.
The collector and external observer own histories.

g.title: StateSpace
g.text: Y = (u, v) in R^(2m), used inside one solve.
Each solve starts from (z + mu, z - mu).
Only the accepted physical state persists.
This doubling contains physical coordinates only.
Time and conjugate momentum are not state blocks.
These dimensions apply to maps and result records.

g.title: Runtime
g.text: Create a fresh controller and IntegrationCollector.
Validate each accepted interval and state.
save requested samples; report temporal progress.
Merge metadata, metrics, auxiliary output and aliases.
No branch selects a numerical-method class.

g.title: FamilyResources
g.text: The BM4 composition consumes these maps.

g.text: Record basic metrics and optional observations

g.title: Grid
g.text: Yield StepInfo and run.advance(t, state, h).
Interior output: shortened advance from a copy
A shadow sample does not alter the main grid.
Its work is excluded from metrics and observations.
DOP853 and Radau supply a different controller.

g.title: Advance
g.text: BM4 COMPLETE STEP / NO RECORDING SIDE EFFECTS
Return accepted physical coordinates, five metrics
No step index or main/shadow flag is needed.
The coordinator chooses what to collect and observe.
Preserve the input state and fixed-map resources.

g.title: ProjectedStep
g.text: Observation reads the stored converged copies.

g.title: StepRecipe
g.text: Solve one multiplier around the full composition.
Use signed duration b_i h for every stage.
Carry the signed composition clock forward.
There is no projection between the twelve maps.
The stage maps are explicit sequential updates.
The outer multiplier equation makes BM4 implicit.

g.title: Projection
g.text: class operations, t, z, h, solver controls
mu in R^m; initial guess mu = 0.
Input copies: Y_hat = (z + mu, z - mu).
Mapped copies: (u, v) = Psi(t, h, Y_hat).
Correct both outputs: (u + mu, v - mu).
Return their mean as the accepted physical state.
The same mu shifts input and output copies.

g.title: Nonlinear
g.text: BM4 NEWTON LOOP / SHARED BROYDEN SERVICE
local loop in the reduced BM4 solve.
G = [I, -I]; J = D Psi; K = G J G^T + 2I.
Solve K delta = r; update mu = mu - delta.
J uses exact stage products or centered differences.
Start the reduced Jacobian approximation at 4I.
Update it from secants using residuals only.
An unconverged or singular solve raises an error.
A zero-correction solve still evaluates a residual.

g.title: Maps
g.text: Evaluate all twelve stages with events disabled.
with particle blocks and exact coupling derivatives.
Finite difference: differentiate the complete map.
Broyden does not request map Jacobians.
Each analytic factor uses its own stage state/time.

g.title: Stages
g.text: SHARED GC MAPS / BM4 SIGNED COMPOSITION
Let d = b_i h; tau = current composition clock.
f is the physical vector field.
C_d is the exact harmonic coupling of both copies.
Direct (even stages), evaluated at tau + d
v = v + d f(tau + d, u)
u = u + d f(tau + d, v)
After either map: tau = tau + d.
Negative durations also move the clock backward.
All twelve signed durations sum to h.

g.title: Legend
g.text: Thick arrows between phase headers: overall lifecycle; phases 04 and 05 repeat together for each main step.
Thin solid arrows: calls or required data. Dotted blue arrows: returned values. Dashed purple arrows: optional events.
A hollow diamond means a record contains another record. Red dashed arrows indicate failure propagation.
Card subtitles distinguish actual APIs from inline operations and numerical contracts.
One accepted physical state in R^m; two temporary copies in R^(2m); one multiplier in R^m.
One reduced Hairer projection surrounds the complete twelve-stage direct/adjoint composition.
The nonlinear solve can evaluate the full base cycle many times before accepting one physical step.
Newton and Broyden solve the same equation. The local Newton loop uses analytic or finite-difference map Jacobians.
Shadow advances and optional cycle reconstruction preserve the main trajectory and its accepted-solve statistics.

g.title: Recording
g.text: ONE RUN / REQUESTED SAMPLES + ACCEPTED METRICS
Copy metric rows with stable keys and shapes.
Never store method details or observer events.
Rejected adaptive trials have no accepted row;
their numerical work belongs to the accepted step.

g.title: EventBuilder
g.text: Require the replayed mapped state to match exactly.
Preserve all twelve signed stage times and states.
Bind map_state(candidate) to the same solve.
Shadow samples never request this builder.

g.title: PhaseOutput
g.text: Finalize, validate and interpret the trajectory

g.title: Data
g.text: extracts the physical state and optional energy.
Export never repeats the numerical projection.
Internal and physical dimensions may differ.
Return to the original SimulationRunner call.
Only the requested trajectory is exposed by default.

Check shape, finiteness and packed layout.
